Designing Possibilities. Connecting Worlds. Creating Impact.

About Stephanie

Some people see what is. Others see what could be.

Stephanie R. Owens has built a career at the intersection of those two perspectives — recognizing potential, connecting people and ideas, and creating the strategy, structure, and experiences that bring ambitious visions to life.

With more than 25 years of experience spanning business, creative industries, culture, philanthropy, and hospitality, Stephanie brings a distinctive combination of commercial insight, entrepreneurial thinking, organizational leadership, and creative vision. Throughout her career, she has moved fluidly between the corporate, entrepreneurial, and nonprofit worlds, bringing together experience in global retail, entertainment, organizational leadership, and the development of meaningful experiences.

She has built businesses, managed multimillion-dollar commercial portfolios, developed brands and partnerships, led organizations through significant transitions, and produced events and experiences that bring people together. Her work has included building an independent image consultancy and establishing Island Def Jam's first in-house styling team, leading global merchandising and product development divisions at Gap Inc. and Macy's, founding a youth development organization, and guiding a major cultural institution through a period of extraordinary change.

Having lived and worked abroad and built a career across the United States, Stephanie brings a global perspective informed by firsthand experience navigating different cultures, languages, and communities. That perspective helps her recognize how culture and context shape opportunity, build connections across borders, and create experiences that resonate with people from different backgrounds.

Through Aya Collective, Stephanie brings this breadth of experience to businesses, organizations, entrepreneurs, and individuals looking to turn ambitious ideas into meaningful outcomes. From shaping the initial vision and developing the strategy to securing resources, managing budgets, building teams, and overseeing execution, she understands what it takes to move an idea from concept to reality. Her approach combines executive-level perspective with hands-on leadership — bringing together the people, resources, and expertise needed to make things happen.

Career & leadership

Six chapters, one throughline.

Select any role to read further detail.

Strategic & Operations Consultant Chef Lowell LLC / Eight 17 Collective 2025–Present

Provides strategic and operational leadership across business development, financial planning, organizational growth, and experiential initiatives. Supports the development and execution of new concepts, partnerships, and business opportunities across hospitality and related ventures.

Executive Director National Black Arts Festival 2020–2025

Joined the organization in 2019 and became Executive Director in 2020. Led a major cultural institution through the disruption of the pandemic and a period of significant organizational change. Guided strategic planning, fundraising, partnership development, and operational growth. Through resource development and financial stewardship, helped establish more than $750,000 in organizational reserves by the conclusion of her tenure. Supported more than 200 artists through the Artist Project Fund and other creative programming.

Founder P&J Foundation 2017–2019

Founded a grassroots youth development organization in Vallejo, California, building school-system partnerships and launching the Student to Community mentoring initiative to connect young people with professional guidance, mentorship, and pathways to opportunity.

Global Merchandising & Product Development Gap Inc. and Macy's 2008–2017

Held leadership roles in global merchandising and product development, managing large-scale product portfolios, budgets, and teams. Led product strategy and collection development across major retail divisions, including Gap Global Girls and Boys, with a combined portfolio value of $236 million. Launched product collections associated with more than $75 million in margin.

Founder Oshare' LLC 2001–2008

Founded Oshare', LLC, an independent styling and image consultancy serving artists and entertainment clients. Built and led Island Def Jam Music Group's first in-house styling team, shaping artist image and overseeing wardrobe, photo shoots, music videos, and special events. Clients included Dave Chappelle, Kanye West, Ludacris and more.

Sales & Marketing Island Def Jam Music Group 1999–2002

Worked across music sales and marketing, contributing to artist and label initiatives within the entertainment industry. Her international experience also included time in Japan, where she taught English and engaged with the music industry through Def Jam Japan.

The Aya philosophy

Every great idea begins with a vision.

But bringing that vision to life takes more than a good plan — it takes the experience to navigate the challenges, the leadership to bring people together, and the ability to manage the resources, relationships, and work required to make it happen.

Aya brings both dimensions together: the strategic and operational capability to get things done, and the curiosity, cultural understanding, and collaborative spirit to honor the vision behind the work.

Whether helping an individual explore new possibilities, an entrepreneur build a business, or an organization bring an ambitious initiative to life, Aya partners with clients from the earliest spark of an idea through planning, development, and execution.

Together, we turn ambitious ideas into meaningful work, extraordinary experiences, and lasting impact.

Work directly with Stephanie.

Every client relationship is personal. The same hands-on leadership shaping the vision is present throughout the process, from the first conversation to the final execution.
